messages:
From: Kim Tran <kim@foundersbridge.vc>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@foundersbridge.vc
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Inquiry: can we convert incubator credits into a committed discount for Dedicated?

Hi Marcus,

Quick question from the Founders Bridge ops team — our startups received a pool of promo credits (accelerator stipend) that many of them will consume quickly during onboarding. A few of our teams are interested in moving from the promo pool to a predictable Dedicated capacity commitment because of steady inference needs.

Is there a program or one-off exception where credits can be applied as a partial upfront payment that converts into a % discount on a 6–12 month Dedicated commitment? Procurement is asking for a simple conversion mechanic so we can show finance the effective unit price.

Also: any constraints on using credits for onboarding vs. committing to Reserved capacity? We may need a written note (SOW/one-pager) for our internal stakeholders.

Thanks — appreciate any creative options.

Kim

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Kim Tran <kim@foundersbridge.vc>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 11:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Inquiry: can we convert incubator credits into a committed discount for Dedicated?

Hi Kim — thanks for the clear ask and context. We can definitely do something creative here; below is a pragmatic option that balances our runway and your portfolio flexibility.

Proposal (summary):
- Credits -> Bridge Payment: Founders Bridge provides an upfront allocation of accelerator credits (we treat them as a prepayment).
- Conversion Window: Within 90 days of execution, credits may convert to a committed Dedicated commitment. Conversion is applied as a one-time credit against the first 3 months of the Dedicated invoice.
- Conversion Ratio: Credits applied convert at a 60% rate to committed spend (i.e., $1,000 in credits = $600 of committed spend credited).
- Commitment Discount: For teams that convert to a 6-month Dedicated contract within the window, offer a sliding discount on committed unit price: 5% for 6 months, 8% for 9 months, 12% for 12 months. Discount stacks with the conversion credit.
- Governance: One conversion event per org. Conversion non-transferable between separate customers.

Operational asks from your side:
- Confirm list of teams/org IDs eligible (we'll produce an eligible-org CSV).
- Procurement will need SOW + commitment addendum. I've attached a draft pricing proposal and conversion matrix for clarity.

Risks/notes:
- We need legal sign-off for any deviation from standard promo rules.
- We treat credits as revenue recognition that may affect how much we can convert; the 60% conversion rate is intended to balance gross-to-net and churn risk.

If you'd like, Ben can propose a narrower pilot (2–3 teams) to run the process end-to-end before broad roll-out. Laura, would this require an approval path?

Next steps suggested:
1) Confirm eligible teams and desired conversion percentage.
2) Redwood to provide SOW addendum + pricing table.
3) Procurement sends standard PO or DocuSign to accept terms.

Happy to hop on a quick 20-minute call tomorrow to walk through the matrix.

Best,

Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Inquiry: can we convert incubator credits into a committed discount for Dedicated?

Adding a complementary option from a sales packaging perspective — a lighter-weight path for teams that want Dedicated but don't want to sign long term immediately:

Pilot Convert + Early Renewal Incentive:
- Pilot Commitment: 3-month Dedicated minimum (smaller GPU pool) funded by converted credits at a 50% conversion rate.
- If team renews/expands to 6+ months within 120 days of pilot end, we credit an additional one-time 6% off the next invoice (effectively boosting conversion economics).
- This gives teams runway to validate traffic, and gives Redwood an upsell path.

Why this might work: Founders Bridge concerns often center on teams' runway & procurement cycle — pilots lower the barrier, renewal incentive drives conversions without a long immediate legal commitment.

Open question: can we standardize the renewal incentive in the SOW language so procurement sees the clear metric?

Happy to run a pricing sensitivity with Marcus if you send 2–3 example consumption profiles.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0137

Thanks Marcus and Ben — this looks solid. A few internal ops notes / approval items to expedite:

1) Approval needed from Revenue Ops for conversion mechanic (we'll need to document accounting treatment). I'll loop in RevOps and Legal with the attached SOW template.
2) Recommend we pilot Ben's "Pilot Convert + Early Renewal Incentive" for up to 5 teams from Founders Bridge. Limit: total converted credit exposure <= $75k for the pilot.
3) Add a clause: if org churns within 60 days of conversion, Redwood reserves the right to reclaim up to 30% of converted value as a protective clause. (This protects against rapid churn and gaming.)

Kim — if you can confirm 2–5 candidate startups and an estimated total credit pool, we'll produce a pilot SOW (DocuSign-ready) and provide a projected unit-price table so finance can model.

I'll prepare an internal approval note and loop Legal + RevOps today. Marcus, please attach sample consumption profiles when you have them.
